November 2, 2026 · Released
### Keyslam 1.0.1

Five new sound packs, 15 in all: Unicomp, Model F, Gateron Red, MX Black and Rainy 75, each cut from a CC0 recording on Freesound.
#### New sound packs

- Unicomp (buckling spring): a Unicomp buckling-spring keyboard. From “Typing on a keyboard” by SamsterBirdies on Freesound.
- Model F (buckling spring): an early-1980s IBM Model F XT. From “IBM Model F keyboard typing” by Fractal_ on Freesound.
- Gateron Red (linear): Gateron Red switches on a GMMK TKL. From “Typing on a mechanical keyboard” by IRF1010N on Freesound.
- MX Black (linear): Cherry MX Black switches on a Leopold FC980M PD. From “leopold fc980m pd cherry mx black.flac” by ujonathan on Freesound.
- Rainy 75 (mechanical): a Rainy 75 keyboard; the uploader doesn't name its switches. From “Typing on a rainy 75” by Techrul on Freesound.
- Like the other keyboard packs, each new pack is cut from one real typing recording released as CC0, with separate takes for Space, Return and Delete, key-up sounds, and real strikes sorted by natural loudness into soft, medium, hard and slam bands. Every pack plays at the same loudness, -28 LUFS.
#### Changes

- The Sound grid in the menu now fits all 15 boards, one line per board, with the selected board's kind and description underneath.
- Each pack's credits name every source recording once.
#### Updating from 1.0.0

- There is no built-in updater. Download 1.0.1 from the website's download page, quit Keyslam from its menu, and replace the copy in Applications.
- Your license still works: 1.0.1 is a free update with nothing more to pay. The trial date, license and settings stay where they were.
#### Requirements

- macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel.

November 2, 2026 · Released
### Keyslam 1.0.0

First public release: adds an on/off shortcut and Quiet during calls. Universal (Apple silicon and Intel), Developer ID-signed and notarized by Apple.
#### New

- Turn sounds on and off from any app with a global shortcut, ⌃⌥⌘K by default. In the menu you can switch it off or pick ⌃⌥⌘S, ⌃⌥⌘M or ⌃⌥⌘T instead; if another app already uses the shortcut, the menu says so. No extra permission.
- Quiet during calls, on by default: sounds pause while any app is using the microphone and come back when it's free. Keyslam doesn't record or open the microphone and asks for no microphone permission; it only checks whether the input device is in use.
#### Release

- One universal app for Apple silicon and Intel, Developer ID-signed (Venture Deals, Co.), notarized and stapled by Apple.
#### Requirements

- macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel.
#### Not in this version

- No built-in updater; new versions come from the website's download page.

November 2, 2026 · Pre-release
### Keyslam 0.1.0

The first build: 10 real keyboard and typewriter packs, force sensing on MacBooks with the motion sensor, and an offline license. It was never made public.
#### Sounds

- 10 packs, each cut from one real CC0 recording on Freesound: MX Blue, MX Brown, MX Red, Topre, Leopold, WhiteFox, Vintage Technics, Laptop, Selectric, Olivetti.
- The keyboard packs have separate takes for regular keys and for Space, Return and Delete, plus key-up sounds. The two typewriters have no key-up sounds and ring a bell on Return.
- Real strikes sorted by natural loudness into four strength bands: soft, medium, hard and slam (the hardest ~8%). Each band is leveled toward its own target.
- Every pack leveled to the same loudness, -28 LUFS, so switching boards keeps the volume about the same.
- Each key keeps its own take and pitch, and stereo placement follows the key's position.
#### Force sensing

- On MacBook Pro with M1 Pro or M1 Max and later, and MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M2 and later, the app reads the motion sensor about 800 times a second and blends the two nearest bands for each keystroke.
- A Sensitivity slider and a four-segment meter that shows how hard the last key landed.
- On Macs without the sensor, or with force sensing switched off, a Soft / Medium / Hard / Slam picker sets a fixed strength.
#### The app

- Native Swift menu-bar app with a C real-time audio core and an audio buffer of about 5 ms. About 12 MB installed with every pack included.
- Audio and the motion sensor switch off after 3 idle minutes; the next key wakes them.
- Options: key release sounds, stereo by key position, open at login, and a Preview button.
- Custom packs: WAV, AIFF or FLAC files with a pack.json, dropped into the Packs folder.
- If Input Monitoring is missing, the menu shows Open Settings, and Relaunch Keyslam when macOS needs a restart of the app.
#### Buying and privacy

- 7-day free trial with everything unlocked, no account and no card. The trial date is kept in the Keychain.
- $3.99 once through Stripe Checkout. The Ed25519-signed key is verified offline; the Activate button on the purchase page opens the app and activates the key.
- Remove License From This Mac deletes the key locally. Nothing counts activations.
- No network connections and no analytics.
#### Requirements

- macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel.
#### Not in this version

- No system-wide shortcut to switch sounds on and off; use the switch in the menu bar.
- Sounds don't pause on their own during calls.
- No built-in updater; new versions will come from the website's download page.

### How updates reach you

Keyslam has no update checker, because the app makes no network connections. New versions will be posted on the download page and listed here with the date and what changed. What the app does and doesn't send is in the privacy policy.

### Updates: questions

How do I update Keyslam?
There is no built-in updater, so the app never checks for updates on its own. When a new version is out, download it from the download page, quit Keyslam from its menu, and replace the copy in Applications.

Does reinstalling or updating reset my trial or license?
No. The trial start date and your license live in your Mac's Keychain, not inside the app, so they survive a reinstall. Your settings stay too.

Do updates cost extra?
No. One $3.99 payment covers free updates and every future official pack; see how the lifetime license works.

# Contact Keyslam: Support, Licenses and Press

Your message and email go to our own server (a Cloudflare Worker), not to a helpdesk company. We use them only to reply. Privacy details.

- Topic | What to send | Read first |

- No sound? Open the Keyslam menu and read the line under its name. The no-sound guide matches each message to a fix.

- Common questions about calls, Bluetooth, shortcuts and other Macs are answered in the FAQ.

- Refunds: a full refund within 14 days if Keyslam doesn't work for you. Replying to your Stripe receipt works as well as this form.

- Who you're writing to: Keyslam is made by Samson and sold by Venture Deals, Co. More on the about page.

### Contacting Keyslam

How do I recover a lost license key?
Use the lost-key form on this page. Enter the email you paid with and the receipt number from your Stripe receipt (it looks like 1234-5678; your card's last 4 digits also work). If they match a purchase, the key appears right away. Paste it into Keyslam under “I have a license key”.

Is there a Keyslam support email address?
Not a public one yet. Use the contact form, and we'll reply by email. If you bought Keyslam, replying to your Stripe receipt reaches us too.

Where do I report a mistake on your comparison pages?
Here. Pick “Something else”, name the app and the fact, and link the source. Prices and trials change often, and we fix our comparison when they do.

# Keyboard Sound App No Sound on Mac? Keyslam Fixes
URL: https://keyslam.com/help/no-sound/
Updated: 2026-11-02

Help
## No sound from Keyslam? Here's how to fix it

Most silent keyboards come down to four things: permission, the Sounds switch, the output device, or the trial. The Keyslam menu tells you which in one line.
Download for MacTry it in your browser →
Updated November 2, 2026

Short answer: click the keyboard icon in the menu bar and read the line under “Keyslam”. “Needs Input Monitoring access” means macOS permission; “Off” means the Sounds switch or its shortcut; “Paused while the mic is in use” means an app is using the microphone; “Trial ended” means the trial is over. If it names a board and still no sound plays, check your Mac's output device and volume. Bluetooth headphones add their own delay.

### What the Keyslam menu is telling you

- Line under Keyslam | What it means | Fix |
- “Needs Input Monitoring access” | macOS hasn't let Keyslam notice key presses yet. | Click Open Settings in the orange card and switch Keyslam on. If Relaunch Keyslam appears, click it. |
- “Off” | The Sounds switch at the top right of the menu is off, or the on/off shortcut (⌃⌥⌘K by default) was pressed. | Switch it back on, or press the shortcut again. |
- “Paused while the mic is in use” | Quiet during calls is on and an app is using the microphone: a call, a recording or dictation. | Sounds come back when that app lets go of the mic. To keep them playing anyway, untick Quiet during calls in the menu. |
- “Trial ended” | The 7-day trial is over, so the switch is greyed out. | Buy Keyslam, or click I have a license key and paste yours. |
- A board name, like “MX Blue · Force sensing on” or “MX Blue · Fixed strength” | Keyslam is listening and playing. | The sound is going somewhere you can't hear. Check the output device and volume below. |
- Red text under the boards | A board couldn't load, usually a custom pack. | See “A custom pack is silent or missing” below. |

### The 30-second check

- Open the menu. Click the keyboard icon in the menu bar. A filled icon means Keyslam is active.

- Check the switch. The switch at the top right turns all sounds on and off.

- Press Preview. It's next to SOUND. If you hear a short typing phrase, audio works and the problem is key input. If not, it's output or volume.

- Check the Mac's sound. Make sure the Mac isn't muted and the right output is selected in Control Center › Sound.

- Turn Keyslam up. Its volume slider starts at about half. Drag it to the right.

### Match the symptom

- What you notice | Most likely cause | Section |
- Sounds switch on, but Preview is silent too | Output device, volume or mute | Output and volume |
- Preview plays, typing is silent | Input Monitoring | Input Monitoring |
- Sound arrives late | Bluetooth headphones or speakers | Bluetooth and AirPods |
- First key after a break is late | Audio waking after 3 idle minutes | After a pause or sleep |
- Silent in one place only | A password field or Secure Keyboard Entry | Keys that stay silent |
- Silent during calls or recordings | Quiet during calls (on by default) | What the menu is telling you |
- Every key sounds soft | Sensitivity set too low | External keyboards and force |
- Strength never changes | An external keyboard, or force sensing switched off | External keyboards and force |

### Input Monitoring

macOS only lets an app notice key presses in other apps after you allow Input Monitoring. Keyslam asks on first launch, as the install steps and requirements show. Until it's allowed, the menu shows an orange card: “Keyslam needs Input Monitoring”.

- Click Open Settings in that card. It opens System Settings › Privacy & Security › Input Monitoring.

- Switch Keyslam on. macOS may ask for your password.

- Go back to the menu. If a Relaunch Keyslam button appears, click it. Keyslam shows it when the permission is on but macOS still won't deliver keys after a few seconds, which a fresh start fixes.

After a macOS update or a new copy of the app: if Keyslam is switched on in the list but the menu still asks for access, select Keyslam in the list, remove it with the minus (−) button, then quit and reopen Keyslam and allow it again. This clears a stale entry.

Keyslam's keyboard tap is listen-only: it can see that a key went down, but it can't type, change or block anything. More in what Input Monitoring lets an app see.

### Output and volume

- Keyslam plays through the Mac's current output, the one picked in Control Center › Sound or System Settings › Sound › Output. When you plug in headphones or connect AirPods, it follows the switch on its own.

- The Mac's volume still applies. If the Mac is muted or turned all the way down, Keyslam is silent too.

- Keyslam's slider is a mix level on top. It starts at about half and goes to about twice that level at the right end, but it can't go past the Mac's own volume.

- Check where the sound is going. If the output is a monitor, dock or interface with nothing plugged in, you won't hear it. Pick the built-in speakers to test.

### Bluetooth and AirPods delay

Bluetooth headphones and speakers hold audio in a buffer before they play it, so short sounds like keystrokes arrive noticeably late. Keyslam's own audio buffer is about 5 ms; the extra delay comes from the wireless link, and Keyslam can't remove it. For the snappiest feel, use the built-in speakers or wired headphones.

#### Listening test

Type here with your headphones, then with the Mac's speakers

The button reads what your browser reports for the current output. Browsers add their own buffering, so the number is higher than Keyslam's; compare devices, not apps.

### After a pause or sleep

After 3 minutes without typing, Keyslam switches its audio and the motion sensor off so your Mac can idle and sleep normally. The next key wakes them, so that first sound can be a little late while the audio device starts. When the Mac wakes from sleep, Keyslam reopens its audio and sensor on its own, or with your next key if they had already switched off. If it stays silent, turn the Sounds switch off and on again.

### External keyboards and force sensing

- Every keyboard plays. Built-in, USB and Bluetooth keyboards all trigger sounds.

- Force sensing feels the MacBook's case, so keys on an external keyboard play at your usual strength rather than following how hard you hit them.

- No Force switch? If the FORCE section says force sensing needs a MacBook with the motion sensor, your Mac doesn't have one. Pick Soft, Medium, Hard or Slam instead. Which MacBooks have the sensor.

- Everything sounds soft? Drag Sensitivity to the right. Higher sensitivity makes the hard and slam bands easier to reach.

### Keys that stay silent

- Password fields. macOS hides those keystrokes from all apps, so they make no sound.

- Secure Keyboard Entry. While an app has it on (Terminal has it in its app menu), macOS hides all keystrokes from other apps, and Keyslam goes quiet everywhere. Turn it off when you don't need it.

- Holding a key plays one sound, not a stream. Keyslam ignores auto-repeat.

- Mouse clicks don't make sounds. Keyslam only plays keyboard sounds.

### The trial ended

After 7 days the menu says “Your free trial has ended” and the Sounds switch is greyed out. Buy a $3.99 lifetime license, or click I have a license key and paste your key. Lost it? Recover it on the contact page with your Stripe receipt number.

### A custom pack is silent or missing

Custom packs live in ~/Library/Application Support/Keyslam/Packs. Open it from the menu with Packs Folder…. Each pack is a folder with a pack.json and its WAV, AIFF or FLAC files. Keyslam rescans the folder every time you open the menu.

- Not in the list? The folder has no pack.json, or it isn't valid JSON with formatVersion, id, name, kind and groups.

- Red “couldn't load” text? A file named in pack.json is missing or unreadable, a path points outside the folder, there's no usable key group, or the decoded audio is over 96 MB.

- A built-in board changed? A custom pack with the same id replaces the built-in one.

- Only one strength? That's fine. Missing bands fall back to the nearest one you provided, played a little softer or louder.

A minimal working pack.json looks like this (the "up" line is optional):

{
"formatVersion": 1,
"id": "my-board",
"name": "My Board",
"kind": "Linear",
"groups": {
"alpha": {
"down": { "medium": ["key-1.wav", "key-2.wav"] },
"up": ["up-1.wav"]
}
}
}

Group names are alpha, space, enter, backspace and modifier; missing groups use alpha. Band names are soft, medium, hard and slam.

### Still no sound?

Send us a message with your macOS version, Mac model and the exact line under “Keyslam” in the menu. Common questions about calls, shortcuts and other Macs are in the FAQ.

### No sound: questions

Why did Keyslam stop after a macOS update?
An update to macOS or to Keyslam can leave a stale Input Monitoring entry: Keyslam looks switched on in System Settings, but macOS no longer honors it. Select Keyslam in Privacy & Security › Input Monitoring, remove it with the minus button, then quit and reopen Keyslam and allow it again.

How do I check the sound delay?
Type in the test box on this page with your Bluetooth headphones, then switch to the Mac's built-in speakers and type again. If the lag disappears on the speakers, it comes from the Bluetooth link. In a current version of Chrome, Firefox or Safari, the delay button shows the browser's own estimate for each device.

Why is there no sound when I type a password?
macOS hides keystrokes in password fields from all apps, including Keyslam, so those keys stay silent on purpose. The same happens everywhere while an app has Secure Keyboard Entry turned on.

# Keyslam Press Kit: Fact Sheet, Logo, Screenshots

Press
## Keyslam press kit

Everything you need to write about Keyslam: the facts, ready-to-use descriptions, a founder quote, the logo, screenshots and keycap art. All checked on November 2, 2026.
Download for MacTry it in your browser →
Updated November 2, 2026

Short answer: Keyslam is a Mac menu-bar app that plays real keyboard and typewriter recordings as you type. On MacBooks with Apple's motion sensor, it feels how hard each key lands and picks real strikes to match. It costs $3.99 once after a 7-day free trial, and the app makes no network connections.

### Fact sheet

- Fact | Detail |
- Name | Keyslam (one word). For clarity: “Keyslam, the Mac keyboard sound app” |
- What it is | A native macOS menu-bar app that plays real keyboard and typewriter recordings on every keystroke, in any app |
- Made by | Samson, Founder |
- Sold by | Venture Deals, Co., through Stripe Checkout |
- Status | Version 1.0.1, available to download; see the install steps and requirements |
- Price | $3.99 once: lifetime license, free updates, all current and future packs |
- Free trial | 7 days, everything unlocked, no account, no card |
- License | Personal; use it on all the Macs you own. Full refund within 14 days if it doesn't work for you |
- Requires | macOS 13 Ventura or later, Apple silicon or Intel; about 16 MB installed |
- Force sensing | MacBook Pro with M1 Pro or M1 Max and later; MacBook Air and MacBook Pro with M2 and later. About 800 sensor readings a second |
- Other Macs | Every sound works at a strength you pick: Intel Macs, desktops, the M1 MacBook Air and the 13-inch M1 MacBook Pro |
- Sounds | 15 packs: MX Blue, MX Brown, MX Red, MX Black, Gateron Red, Topre, Leopold, WhiteFox, Rainy 75, Unicomp, Model F, Vintage Technics, Laptop, Selectric, Olivetti |
- Recordings | Third-party CC0 recordings from Freesound, each credited by name |
- Audio | C real-time audio core, about 5 ms buffer; every pack leveled to -28 LUFS |
- Privacy | The app: no network connections, no analytics; Ed25519-signed license verified offline |
- Distribution | Direct download from keyslam.com, not the Mac App Store |

Source of truth for every number here: the app's code and our fact sheet, last verified November 2, 2026. Recordings are credited on the about page.

### Boilerplate

#### Short (51 words)

Keyslam is a Mac menu-bar app that plays real keyboard and typewriter recordings as you type. On MacBooks with Apple's motion sensor, it feels how hard each key lands and picks real strikes to match. It costs $3.99 once after a 7-day free trial, and the app makes no network connections.

#### Long (104 words)

Keyslam is a native macOS menu-bar app that plays real keyboard and typewriter recordings as you type. Its 15 packs, from Cherry MX switches, an IBM Model F and a Topre HHKB to an IBM Selectric II, are each cut from one CC0 recording on Freesound and sorted into soft, medium, hard and slam bands of real strikes. On MacBooks with Apple's motion sensor, it reads the accelerometer about 800 times a second to match each keystroke; other Macs use a strength you pick. It runs on macOS 13 Ventura or later, costs $3.99 once after a 7-day trial, and makes no network connections.

### Founder quote

“Every Keyslam pack starts as one real typing recording that someone shared on Freesound as CC0. We sort its strikes from the softest to the hardest, and on a MacBook with the motion sensor the app picks from those bands on every keystroke. It costs $3.99 once, and the app itself never connects to the internet.”
Samson, Founder, Keyslam

### How to describe Keyslam accurately

- The sounds are real recordings: each pack is one typing take, with its real strikes sorted by natural loudness into soft, medium, hard and slam bands. Slam is the hardest ~8% of strikes in that take. Please don't describe the bands as separate sessions recorded at different strengths.

- Force sensing works on MacBooks with Apple's motion sensor. Other apps react to typing force too, so please don't call Keyslam the only one. On Macs without the sensor, users pick the strength.

- The recordings are third-party CC0 recordings from Freesound, credited to the people who made them.

- Availability: the download is live.

- Privacy: the app makes no network connections and has no analytics. Buying happens in the browser through Stripe.

How the bands are made, step by step: About Keyslam. What is in each version: release notes.
